correctness.rationale: The 20 quaternary 3-column minors establish [6,3,4]; Hermitian matrix identity constrains intersections of pairs of weight-four supports. Exhaustive intersection-case counting gives 15+180+45=240 distinct twelve-coordinate binary two-space supports. Binary averaging proves any three-space needs at least 14 coordinates, preventing duplicates and higher-rank masks. The weight enumerator and an incidence double count then give 8748 and 9576. The included checker independently exhausts all 18564 erasure masks via binary matrix rank and direct codeword inclusion, plus all 651 binary two-spaces.

value.rationale: For a code used with locality-two repair, minimum distance eight only guarantees unique correction through seven erasures; the first size at which four-way ambiguity is possible is the natural second support threshold. Exact counts of 240 four-way patterns, 8748 two-way patterns, 9576 uniquely decodable patterns and their 15/180/45 block geometries quantify near-threshold erasure reliability, a mathematically motivated invariant not reducible to a published ordinary weight table. The finite, exact result needs no downstream asymptotic theorem.
